en: For what fault of the Kyrgyz
Have you tormented their lives so cruelly?
For as long as anyone remembers,
Your frenzy has never ceased,
Nor have you had your fill of drinking blood.
Plundering tribes and slaughtering people,
You have never ceased your strife.
You steeped your spear in blood
And would heed no word spoken to you.
You crossed ridges and mountain passes,
Sowing turmoil and strife.
However often I warned you, you would not change;
For as long as anyone remembers,
You have never ceased your violence.
As I searched for you through turmoil,
You came yourself, Sarybay;
The time has come to clash
And joust with me, Sarybay.
Eager to unleash another battle,
Your eyes straining wide,
You came yourself, Sarybay.
The time has come to strike unfalteringly with the sword
And stand amid the havoc,
The time has come, Sarybay.
Rousing the people and gathering an army,
Swelling your host to myriad ranks,
You came yourself, Sarybay.
Now the time has come for you to fall and die,
To behold the broad realm
From which none return,
The time has come, Sarybay.
Called the son of a demon,
Your fame spread among the people;
You subjugated the whole world,
And your violence overflowed.
I shall answer your violence;
My name is Kuyaly,
And I have come from afar to find you thus.
May your oath strike you—stand your ground!
If you are a hero and a warrior,
If you are brave Sarybay,
Do not lose your wits,
And do not flee from what lies ahead!”
So saying, Kuyaly
Gripped her deadly steel spear,
Twisting it firmly in her hand.
“The flesh of his breast is my mark,
The edge of his lung my measure;
His heart has fallen into my hand,
And this swaggering boar
Shall fall at this very spot,” she said,
And Kuyaly thrust her spear.
Then Sarybay,
Bellowing and roaring,
Bent down the spearhead.
His weapon was a steel battle-axe;
The demon-born infidel’s
Strength was formidable.
He seized the battle-axe
And, not letting the spear approach,
Beat it aside and held his ground.
When the deflected spear passed by
And Sarybay had escaped it,
Sarybay bristled with menace
And grew furious.
He overcame
Every danger before him.
Hissing like a dragon,
He roared threateningly;
His shout seemed to split heads,
And the raging boar’s
Bellow seemed to split stones.
His savage wrath poured forth,
His venom set him apart—
Ask no more of Sarybay’s state.
Raging and straining,
He made ready with leveled spear.
“You infidel who ruins nations!
You woman I shall seize!” he cried,
And raged in a frenzy,
While his host surged without rest.
He braced himself and took aim,
His mouth like a burning ember,
His valor fierce, his skill supreme,
His cunning deep, his power unmatched.
His heroism was extraordinary,
His strength beyond measure,
His menace great, his venom strong.
“At the sight of the infidel I am as good as dead,”
And he gave up hope for his fly-like soul.
Sarybay was calamity itself;
Such was the battle he unleashed.
Ask no more of Sarybay’s state:
When angered, fury choked him,
And any mortal marked for death
Who met that infidel’s menace was doomed.
He thundered in a frenzy,
Strained and hurled vile words.
As he came in wrath,
His savage courage stood revealed;
One glance at the dreadful swine
Showed the look of one ready to kill.
He could not refrain from wreaking havoc;
The troops fled in every direction,
Scattering in panic and ruin.
That infidel Sarybay’s
True ferocity appeared,
And his mind fixed wholly upon battle.
Raging and working himself up,
He spoke in many ways:
“You frenzied champion,
A girl grown old while still calling herself a maid,
A girl who has lived too long,
A girl who mouths deceitful words—
Warrior girl, you have set my soul aflame!
No caravan of yours ever came over the pass;
You have no feud so grievous
As to avenge forty generations of fathers.
No caravan of yours ever journeyed here before;
You have no feud of a hundred forefathers
For which to track my yellow trail
And pursue me until you turn pale.
There was no quarrel between us,
No cause for us to feud,
No word from your protector
Calling us to fight to the death.
No caravan of yours came from Talas,
And your protector has no vengeance to seek.
I shall cast a chill lasso
Over Zhelzhetpes, whom none can take by asking;
Zhelzhetpes, who yields to none he sees,
I shall openly drag away.
I shall make you plead before me in vain,
And force you to become my wife.
I shall wreak boundless ruin;
My wrath has risen and stiffened me,
And I shall make your father my plunder.
If fate decrees it, let me die;
This wretched Kalmak has gone mad—
I shall deliver punishment into her hands.
Striking hard at her spirit,
I shall now finish her,
Spew forth my poisonous venom,
And dig out her roots.
I shall show my savagery,
And die fighting if I must.
I shall crush the life beneath me
And tear apart her rib bones.”
“Here is havoc, if that is what you crave;
Here is the fine spectacle of slaughter!
Here is my she-dog of a girl;
Here is the one who challenged me!”
He struck Tor-Kyzyl on the flank,
And took up his blue-steel spear.
His eyes bulged as if they would leap out,
His jaws seemed ready to split when he bit down;
His face was like a burning ember
As he gathered courage and took aim.
Raging and bellowing,
He had hunted down many khans;
The solid black earth itself
Had smoked beneath his vast weight.
He had crushed multitudes—
The madman, brave Sarybay,
Had come seeking combat,
And many thousands of giants had died,
Struck down by the calamity he unleashed.
In many lands he slaughtered peoples;
Sarybay had amassed blood,
And journeyed for many years,
Gathering clouds of dust behind him.
Ask no more of Sarybay’s state:
Bull-necked and camel-thighed,
He ruined all who grappled with him,
Subjugated all whom he confronted,
And stirred conflict throughout the world.
His looming shadow spread across the earth;
At the words, “Sarybay is coming,”
Even speechless infants
Lying in their cradles fell silent.
His wrath was known among the people;
Any mortal who went against him
Was known to despair of life.
He hewed down all who encountered him
And devoured all who opposed him.
Such was that knave, brave Sarybay:
No man could advance against him,
And he valued no one’s worth.
Mighty indeed was Sarybay;
Behold what a dreadful one he was.
Like a boar that devastated nations,
When Kuyaly thrust her spear at him,
He cried, “I have taken a spear-blow from a girl!
Blood-soaked bitch, you!”
His face darkened and his aspect changed;
Wrath choked him.
He looked before and behind,
Licking his lips like a hungry wolf.
His lashes burned like embers,
And he poised himself like a darting snake.
Unable to contain his fury,
Sarybay unleashed his wrath.
Under the force of his menace,
When the blackguard grew angry, the earth shook,
And seemed about to collapse.
His shriek rang piercingly,
Like a bolt of lightning;
The breath from his mouth
Was like the embers of burning saxaul.
His fury was unmatched, his venom strong;
Such was the sight of him.
If he charged in wrath,
His assault seemed bound to end all.
His dangling beard
And bushy mustache
Were such that pied crows and magpies
Could fearlessly roost in them.
At nightfall they might lodge there till dawn;
Whoever encountered him would spill blood.
Such was Sarybay’s nature.
He turned Tor-Kyzyl’s head;
Surely God had struck
That hellish, wrathful swine.
Before one could cry out,
He wheeled Tor-Kyzyl around.
With his nine-knobbed steel spear,
Before the nimble woman could pull it round,
And hold it twisted at the ready,
Before Zhelzhetpes could find his bearing
And come straight onto the path,
He thrust his spear without pause…
A great calamity began.
Atop Zhelzhetpes,
The consummate warrior, the lioness,
Was a girl whose strength boiled over,
A girl who had overcome the whole world
Through wrestling and combat.
She neither swayed nor flinched,
And cared nothing if she died.
Sarybay’s thrust,
And all the havoc he wrought,
She did not count worth her boot-tip.
Her heart did not falter,
And the cowardly knave’s spear
She deemed no harder than tumbleweed.
When Sarybay drove in his spear
And it crashed against the warrior maiden,
Yet she did not so much as stir,
Sarybay flew into a rage
And shouted to his vast army:
“Every one of you, swarm over her!
Trample this creature called a woman,
This bitch, into the black earth!
The madwoman is a champion—
Overwhelm her in a mass,
Fall upon her with spears and axes,
